subagents.last_text:
I added one test to `src/auth/token.test.mjs` checking that `resolveToken()` throws when called with no token. The full suite passes with 4 tests and 0 failures, and nothing is committed.

**PRECEDENT.md files found:** there is none in `src/` or at the repo root. The only one that applies is `src/auth/PRECEDENT.md`. The others (`scripts/`, `src/tabs/`, `src/head/`, `src/layout/`) cover other code. The relevant rule:

> ### §explicit-token — the token comes only from the caller
> - Decision: `resolveToken` returns `options.token` or throws. It never reads environment variables or files.
> - Forbidden: falling back to `process.env` (any variable name) or to a dotfile.

This agrees with the task, so there was nothing to stop and report. The file has no rules about test framework or style, and no section for `token.test.mjs`.

**What `resolveToken` does without a token** (I ran it; the source is unchanged):
- Called with no argument, `{}`, `{ token: undefined }`, `{ token: "" }` or `{ token: null }`, it throws `Error` with the message `"resolveToken: pass { token } explicitly"`.

**Diff:**
```diff
--- a/src/auth/token.test.mjs
+++ b/src/auth/token.test.mjs
@@ -5,3 +5,7 @@ import { resolveToken } from "./token.mjs";
 test("returns the explicit token", () => {
   assert.equal(resolveToken({ token: "abc" }), "abc");
 });
+
+test("throws when no token is given", () => {
+  assert.throws(() => resolveToken(), { name: "Error", message: "resolveToken: pass { token } explicitly" });
+});
```
It uses the same `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` style as the existing test, and checks the exact error message the code throws.

**Test run:** `npm test` (which runs `node --test`, on Node v25.9.0):
```
✔ returns the explicit token
✔ throws when no token is given
✔ open assigns increasing keys
✔ close keeps keys
ℹ tests 4 · pass 4 · fail 0 · cancelled 0 · skipped 0 · todo 0
```

**Check that the test can fail:** I copied the module and test to a temp directory and replaced the `throw` with `return undefined`. The new test failed there (1 pass, 1 fail). The temp directory is deleted, the source file was never touched, and `git status` shows only ` M src/auth/token.test.mjs`.

**Surprising:**
- `resolveToken(null)` throws a `TypeError` ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'token')") instead of the intended error, because the `= {}` default only applies to `undefined`. It still throws, so the recorded rule holds, but with an unhelpful message. The task was test-only, so I didn't change or test this.
- The new test covers only the no-argument case. `{}`, `""` and `null` tokens throw the same error but aren't tested; I can add them if you want.
